body.statement: Conditional on an affirmative resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq{:}fixed\text{-}nuisance\text{-}marked\text{-}modulus}\), Low's two-point expected-length inequality gives constants \(c'>0\) and \(n_1\) such that \(\inf_{\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\ge c'K_n^{1/2-\beta}\asymp c'r_n\) for every \(n\ge n_1\); positivity of \(c'\) follows from \(\eta<1-2\alpha\).
body.justification: This is deliberately a conditional corollary: the generic testing reduction is routine once the marked modulus has been constructed.
body.gap: No cited ADRF or blind repeated-measurement paper gives a converse quantifying over every honest measurable band.
body.consumer: Together with the upper theorem, it gives the irreducible resolution of a two-recall ADRF curve.
body.proof_tex:
Assume the affirmative content of \(\mathrm{oeq{:}fixed\text{-}nuisance\text{-}marked\text{-}modulus}\).  Thus there are constants \(\eta\in(0,1-2\alpha)\), \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\), and an integer \(n_0\) such that, for every \(n\ge n_0\), the two laws \(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}\) belong to \(\mathcal M\) and satisfy
\[
 Q_{j,n}:=((P_{j,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},\qquad
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{0,n},Q_{1,n})\le \eta,
 \qquad
 \Delta_n:=\|\mu_{1,n}-\mu_{0,n}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \ge c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}.
\]
Fix \(n\ge n_0\) and an arbitrary band \(\mathcal C_n=(L_n,U_n)\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\).  For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), define the measurable simultaneous-coverage event
\[
 H_{j,n}:=\{L_n(a)\le \mu_{j,n}(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}.
\]
Because \(P_{j,n}\in\mathcal M\), uniform honesty in \(\mathrm{def{:}honest\text{-}bands}\) gives
\[
 Q_{j,n}(H_{j,n})\ge 1-\alpha,
 \qquad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
By the defining event inequality for total variation, \(Q_{0,n}(E)\ge Q_{1,n}(E)-\operatorname{TV}(Q_{0,n},Q_{1,n})\) for every measurable event \(E\).  Taking \(E=H_{1,n}\) and using the displayed total-variation bound yields
\[
 Q_{0,n}(H_{1,n})\ge 1-\alpha-\eta.
\]
The union bound under \(Q_{0,n}\) therefore gives
\[
 Q_{0,n}(H_{0,n}\cap H_{1,n})
 \ge Q_{0,n}(H_{0,n})+Q_{0,n}(H_{1,n})-1
 \ge 1-2\alpha-\eta.
\]
On \(H_{0,n}\cap H_{1,n}\), for every \(a\in I\), the interval \([L_n(a),U_n(a)]\) contains both \(\mu_{0,n}(a)\) and \(\mu_{1,n}(a)\).  Hence
\[
 U_n(a)-L_n(a)\ge |\mu_{1,n}(a)-\mu_{0,n}(a)|
\]
for every \(a\in I\), and taking suprema gives \(W_n\ge\Delta_n\) on that event.  Since \(W_n\ge0\) almost surely by \(\mathrm{def{:}honest\text{-}bands}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{Q_{0,n}}[W_n]
 &\ge E_{Q_{0,n}}[W_n\mathbf 1\{H_{0,n}\cap H_{1,n}\}]\\
 &\ge \Delta_n Q_{0,n}(H_{0,n}\cap H_{1,n})\\
 &\ge (1-2\alpha-\eta)c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The law \(P_{0,n}\) is one member of \(\mathcal M\), so, for this arbitrary honest band,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]
 \ge E_{Q_{0,n}}[W_n]
 \ge c'K_n^{1/2-\beta},
 \qquad
 c':=(1-2\alpha-\eta)c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0,
\]
where strict positivity follows from \(\eta<1-2\alpha\) and \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\).  Taking the infimum over \(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\) proves the asserted all-honest-band lower bound.

It remains only to compare the deterministic scales.  Put \(\gamma:=\beta-1/2>0\), using \(\beta>3/2\), and \(x_n:=\log n/\log\log n\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(x_n\ge2\), and the definition \(K_n=\lfloor x_n\rfloor\) implies
\[
 \frac{x_n}{2}\le K_n\le x_n.
\]
Because \(1/2-\beta=-\gamma\),
\[
 x_n^{-\gamma}\le K_n^{-\gamma}\le 2^\gamma x_n^{-\gamma}.
\]
Finally \(x_n^{-\gamma}=(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}=r_n\).  Therefore \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\asymp r_n\), with constants depending only on \(\beta\), which completes the proof.
